title: Fixed-Time Causal Probability Estimation from Two Inspection Visits with Unknown Gap Density
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield below field, not salvageable in scope, paper_score_ceiling 7<7.4; final math PASS, while novelty and complete-literature priority remain unassessed.
gap_reasons: What is established is a precision frontier up to universal multiplicative constants, with finite-sample honesty, rather than leading constants or practical calibration.

Attainment uses exhaustive finite-lattice search and an upper constant of 2^138, so the prospective icenReg application has no delivered computationally usable implementation or numerical evidence of informative interval lengths.

The flagship matched-frontier theorem is a usable Stat deliverable, but its claimed field-level contribution cannot pass novelty review while the note expressly leaves theorem-level priority unassessed and omits the required Birge1999 priority audit/comparison to the closest fixed-point case-two result class.
proof_attempt_summary: Derived the matched original-record risk and exactly honest connected-interval length frontier across the inspection-gap crossover, strengthened to one exponent-independent procedure. Final D0.5 mathematics passed with no findings after graph dependency and citation repairs; the field research package failed the subfield score ceiling because attainment is an exhaustive finite lattice with enormous constants, without usable implementation or numerical interval evidence, and complete-literature priority remains unassessed. Formalization was not started; no Lean theorem or reusable library module was produced.
tldr: Two visits reveal an event through three categories. A single visit-only certificate selector yields a fixed-time causal probability estimator and connected interval without knowing the inspection density or its gap exponent. On every complete comparable-design class, its risk and expected length have the matched order \(r(n,\kappa)\), and its interval has coverage at least \(0.90\) at each finite sample size. Legal original-record alternatives prove the same-class all-procedure lower bounds. The same procedure adapts without an order penalty through the \(\kappa=0\) logarithmic crossover, including arbitrary unknown drifting exponents. Finite baseline-stratum standardization is the causal application.
gap: Accessible case-two results establish positive-diagonal benchmarks, unknown-design integrated estimation, and convex score machinery, but do not deliver the complete uniform fixed-point rough-design risk-and-honest-length theorem sought here. Original \cite{Birge1999} priority remains externally unverifiable.
fill: The proposal isolates observable-certificate attainment as a first-class open question, couples it to legal all-procedure converses, and makes exact finite-sample causal interval coverage part of the theorem. Finite-confounder adjustment is its application.
